rationale: Engineering leads at 10–500 person product companies are a real, named buyer with active LLM spend—they have budget and the pain (AI output that's 90% done but not shippable) is genuinely frequent and costly. However, the core delivery challenge is the deciding factor: diagnosing and fixing 'polish' gaps (subtle UX inconsistency, edge-case correctness) is hard to automate reliably without significant human judgement per PR/feature, which drags operational_autonomy below the build gate floor of 7. The idea needs a validated, automatable scope (e.g. a narrow visual regression check or a structured code-review checklist prompt) before it's safe to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an automated 'polish audit' layer that accepts a GitHub PR or a set of screenshots/component specs and returns a structured report of UX inconsistencies, missing edge-case handling, and deviation from a defined style guide, delivered via a web form + email. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt pipeline (ingesting diffs, screenshots via vision, and a style-guide doc the customer uploads) connected to a Stripe payment link and a Typeform-style intake form—no coding by the operator. To sell, the factory identifies engineering leads and heads of product at Series A–C SaaS companies via LinkedIn/GitHub signals of active Cursor/Copilot use and sends a cold outreach batch that goes out only after Youval approves it. Delivery is fully automated: customer submits PR link + style guide, Claude processes and emails the report within minutes, Stripe handles billing, and a Claude-powered reply bot handles support questions. The only recurring human touch is approving each outreach batch and reviewing any edge-case support escalations the bot flags as uncertain. The critical risk to validate first: can the audit output be specific and actionable enough that engineers trust it, or does it produce generic advice that gets ignored? Run a 5-customer pilot at ~$50/audit before building further.
notes: operational_autonomy scores 5 (below build gate floor of 7) because 'polish' diagnosis is partially subjective—some per-customer calibration of the style guide and iterative back-and-forth is likely required before output is trustworthy. buildability_with_ai scores 5 (meets the floor of 6 only marginally, effectively borderline) because vision-based UI consistency checking and code edge-case detection require meaningful prompt engineering and potentially multimodal integration work beyond a simple Claude + Stripe setup. Both gates failing means stage is capped at validate. Validate path: offer 5 manual polish audits to engineering leads at a flat fee, deliver with Claude assistance but with Youval reviewing output, and use learnings to tighten the automated pipeline scope before building.
